name: the Future
summary: Ivory structures, living greenery and restrained light fields shape the Administrator's open town.

rules.roads: Use pale ceramic-composite road panels along x, 8 m wide within |z| <= 4, with sparse cyan guidance seams rather than painted asphalt lanes. Street dressing: 22 low parts below 1.2 m, including flush guide emitters, inset drainage slots, repair panels and low edge nodes. Only guide-light parts use glow=true. Keep the middle physically unobstructed; glowing surface lines are navigational graphics, not raised barriers. The glowgrid surface lights its lines only.
rules.walkingEdge: Broad matte tiles occupy |z| 4–6, with a shallow bevelled kerb about 0.08 m high and continuous accessible transitions. A narrow planted drainage seam separates walking from vehicle guidance. Trees and fixtures stand at z 5 without reducing the route to a maze of pods.
rules.lotMarkers: Free lot: 14 parts on a 16 m parcel, with a low ceramic projector near x 4.5, z 4.5 displaying a large empty amber ring below head height. The ring uses glow=true and remains the wordless available symbol; its projector is physical and unlit. Add sparse clover and a few reclaimed aggregate chips. Community lot: 18 parts, with four low anchor blocks and a front projector displaying four connected nodes around one shared centre; only the projected symbol uses glow=true. Keep the build area empty and distinguish public collaboration from private claiming.
rules.boundaries: Claimed lot: 30 parts including the owner marker. Use waist-low woven biocomposite rails between rounded ceramic posts along z -6 and x -6, approximately 0.75 m high and below 1.2 m. Leave the +z front open with a clear entrance gap. Boundaries are tangible and visually permeable, not opaque force walls or glowing cages.
rules.ownerMarker: A front-corner ceramic post has a solid owner-colour insert in #d9534f and projects a small filled household emblem with the exact player name. Only the floating tag uses glow=true; limit bloom so the lettering and red owner accent remain distinct. The tag stays close to its post rather than floating over the building.
rules.lighting: Street light: 12 parts at x 0, z 5, comprising a tapered ivory pillar, a recessed cyan-white emitter and a small directional cap. Only the emitter uses glow=true. Use a broad, calm light source, not a laser beam, giant holographic billboard or neon coating over the entire pillar.
rules.centrepiece: Use 46 parts for a civic hologram beacon on a low physical dais about 4.5 m across. Four ceramic emitter petals surround a floating, faceted seed-like town emblem, with short orbiting light arcs suggesting shared growth. Hologram and arc parts use glow=true; the dais and petals remain matte. Keep the image under about 2.5 m high and transparent enough that the square stays visible.
rules.seating: Use 10 parts for a stable two-person hover seat with a warm biocomposite sitting shell, low back and a discreet ground docking puck. Seat height stays about 0.45 m, including the small levitation gap. Only a narrow lift-status strip uses glow=true; avoid bobbing, inaccessible heights or a giant glowing cushion.
rules.market: Use 34 parts within about 2.6 × 1.6 m for a hovering vending pod with a tangible rounded shell, clear product windows, a fold-out serving tray and small stabiliser nodes. Show fruit, cultured-food packs and reusable refill capsules so its retail role is obvious. Only the small interface and lift emitters use glow=true; the entire pod must not become an unreadable light blob.
rules.trees: Street pair: 32 parts total at x -3 and x 3, z 5; use a tall regenerated shade tree with a tilted trunk and uneven broad crown, and a smaller flowering tree with one long lateral branch. Low root-monitor collars may have a single status pip using glow=true, but leaves and trunks remain natural and unlit. Wild group: 40 parts for a wind-shaped pine, a broad irregular oak and a young willow shrub. Countryside dressing: 16 low sparse parts of clover, native flowers, stones, fallen seed pods and two tiny ecological sensor caps, mostly below 0.35 m. Future ecology is diverse, not cloned topiary or a forest of crystals.
rules.arrival: Use 68 parts for a hover-shuttle stop and vehicle. At z 5 place a thin physical shelter, flush boarding marker and compact arrival glyph; only the glyph and guide strip use glow=true. At z 0, aligned along x, place a roughly 5 m hover shuttle with a rounded ceramic shell, dark windows, visible passenger-door seam and four recessed lift units. Lift emitters use glow=true, but the body does not. Keep boarding at pavement level and avoid a huge landing pad.
rules.crossing: Use 58 parts for a solid-light crossing along z, about 4 m wide, with a continuous shallow translucent deck between physical ceramic bank anchors. Deck light planes and slim guide strips use glow=true; anchors and structural edge pieces remain matte. The traversable deck meets banks about 1 m above water, with low transparent safety rails. Water flows along x across |z| <= 7; show its central 12 m in the river tile and place real bank anchors at z ±7 in the adjoining bank sections. Add native reeds, restored river stones and small erosion-control ribs; the water itself never glows.
rules.camp: Use 86 parts for an android delegation's landed pod with two unfolded shelter wings, making three sheltered zones in total, plus sealed cargo capsules, a compact survey rover and a low shared light core across the river. Only the light core, docking indicators and rover sensor apertures use glow=true. The separate android-envoy leader uses 42 parts including the base figure: an asymmetric ceramic faceplate, dark visor, layered travel tabard and segmented hands, carrying a faceted meteorite token. An unfamiliar orbital-coordinate emblem and a visibly repaired shoulder panel suggest a long journey rather than a local service robot.
rules.people: Use 50 parts total for two residents at x -0.6 and x 0.6, retaining the base figure proportions. One is a human gardener in textured utility knit, soft boots and a short asymmetric jacket, carrying a seed capsule; the other is an android courier with ceramic joints, a cloth wrap-tabard and a compact parcel. Give them different head and hair or visor silhouettes. Keep technological detail broad and functional, with no glowing skin or combat armour.
rules.head: The Administrator uses 46 parts including the base figure. Give them an ivory tailored civic mantle, a dark understated visor band, a large shared-node insignia and three small floating administrative panels arranged beside rather than in front of the face. Panel graphics and the insignia's light inset use glow=true. The controlled panel constellation is the symbol of office, replacing crowns, top hats and ceremonial scissors without turning the head into a military commander.

materials: Warm woven biocomposite rails and seating
Pale modular paving with fine functional seams
Dark non-mirror glazing and visor panels
Soft technical knit and layered travel textiles
Living bark, irregular foliage and restored river stone
avoid: Night-time cyberpunk darkness, heavy bloom and neon on every surface
Modern assets with nothing changed except luminous trim
Glowing water, emissive tree crowns and crystal forests
Perfectly symmetrical trees or sterile all-white landscaping
Opaque force-field boundaries and giant hovering signs
Wheel-based shuttle bodies, steam machinery and medieval office symbols
Combat robots, weaponised civic infrastructure and unreadable swarms of panels
designDirection: Create a bright, optimistic future through pale physical structures, living greenery, restrained luminous interfaces and new functional silhouettes, keeping the chunky toy style and 40° overhead readability. Preserve the 5×5 plan, 16 m parcels, four central community lots and delegation camp across the east river, with all transformations retaining their footprint and purpose. Every advanced object must still reveal its familiar service through a tangible base, entrance, seat, counter or crossing surface rather than becoming an arbitrary hologram. A skyscraper becomes a stepped modular habitat tower, a car becomes a compact hover pod, and a café becomes a rounded refill-and-cultured-tea pavilion with a physical serving hatch. Reserve emission for genuine light-giving parts, keep greenery irregular and use dark apertures to separate ivory forms clearly on stream.
